newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX still seen on course for 3,000 points.
newsitem.headline: German DAX still seen on course for 3,000 points.

text.p: Germany's DAX-30 share index was seen on Monday attempting to climb towards 3,000 points in the coming weeks despite the noticeable slowdown in buying interest that emerged during the afternoon.

The IBIS-DAX index of electronic trade, up 39.21 points at 2,955.02, was unable to add much to the earlier DAX bourse close of 2,954.95 as Wall Street's early gains on Monday were reversed later in the session.
"There's been a slowdown in buying interest here too. I think the 3,000 points is still on, but I would prefer it after a consolidation down to around 2,880 first," one dealer said.
He added that the assault on 3,000 points was more likely next week than this week. US consumer price data due Tuesday were meanwhile being eyed with some caution, others noted.

The overall index was dragged lower by profit-taking in Deutsche Telekom, particularly by U.S. investors, after the barrage of analyst reports that followed expiry on Friday of a regulatory ban on published coverage of the stock.

Its shares slipped 45 pfennigs to 29.86 after earlier hitting a record low of 29.80. Dealers said the commentaries on Telekom had in the main been better than some had expected, with a consensus that the stock was fairly valued at 30 marks.
